import pandas as pd

# Get October trip data to see which dates to target
trips_oct = tables['trips'][(tables['trips']['fish_date_doy'] >= 280) & (tables['trips']['fish_date_doy'] <= 300)].copy()

# Group by DOY to see patterns
oct_summary = trips_oct.groupby('fish_date_doy').agg({
    'yt': ['count', 'mean', 'sum'],
    'anglers': 'mean'
}).round(2)
oct_summary.columns = ['trip_count', 'avg_yt', 'total_yt', 'avg_anglers']
oct_summary['yt_per_angler'] = (oct_summary['total_yt'] / (oct_summary['trip_count'] * oct_summary['avg_anglers'])).round(2)

print("October overnight peak - Best dates for targeting:")
print(oct_summary[oct_summary['avg_yt'] > 20].sort_values('avg_yt', ascending=False))
print("\n")

# Now check the schedule for October to see what boats are available
schedule_oct = tables['schedule'][(tables['schedule']['fish_date_doy'] >= 288) & (tables['schedule']['fish_date_doy'] <= 297) & (tables['schedule']['cls'] == 'overnight')]
print(f"October overnight schedule availability (DOY 288-297):")
print(f"Total overnight trips scheduled: {len(schedule_oct)}")
if len(schedule_oct) > 0:
    sched_by_doy = schedule_oct.groupby('fish_date_doy').size()
    print(sched_by_doy)
